body.statement: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on additional singular and boundary observable laws not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. On each such law, the full-rigidity theorem returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
body.justification: This supporting result validates agreement with the anchor formulas on their regular domain and records the singular and boundary domains handled by the atlas.
body.gap: The 2026 anchor supplies regular inversion formulas but does not state a full-fiber decision procedure on singular support faces or residual-forest boundary strata.
body.consumer: Users of the anchor formulas can verify numerical agreement on regular tables and obtain a defined certification workflow when regular inversions are unavailable.

obligation.what_is_open: Universal coverage of every singular and boundary observable law by the same global structural atlas.
obligation.obstruction: Agreement with the published regular formula and the already-certified all-rank-two boundary datum are available, but the theorem's universal boundary clause is equivalent to the unresolved exhaustiveness of the mixed-support chart list.
obligation.attempted: Matched the regular published PN/PS functional to the cycle target through the established lift, separated the certified forced-zero rank-two boundary branch, and used the residual-forest theorem for the conditional design-B margin problem.
obligation.partial_result: On the regular domain of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki, the cited identification result makes the Appendix expressions (A.28)--(A.33) equal the causal PN/PS pair. The cycle-to-SCM lift preserves that pair as \(\tau_C\); hence, whenever the corresponding full target set is a singleton, its element equals the published expression. Independently, the established rank-two boundary theorem and the established explicit boundary calculation classify the forced-zero datum \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\), while the residual-forest theorem gives an exact conditional elimination of design-B margins. What remains unproved is the universal assertion that the stated structural charts cover every rank-loss, coincident-endpoint, inactive-row, and mixed-support law.
